title: Modulation of Pulmonary Fibrosis by Pulmonary Surfactant-Associated Phosphatidylethanolamine In Vitro and In Vivo
content: Pulmonary surfactant may play a protective role in fibrosing lung diseases by modulating fibroblast activity. In our lab, we found that surfactant enriched with 1,2-dipalmitoyl-rac-glycero-3-phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) induces apoptosis, reduces proliferation, and lowers collagen expression in normal human lung fibroblasts. To explore its therapeutic potential, we developed a natural porcine surfactant enriched with PE (NPPS-PE) obtained by organic synthesis and evaluated its biophysical properties, in vitro antifibrotic effects, and in vivo impact on collagen deposition in a bleomycin-induced fibrosis model. NPPS was extracted via bronchoalveolar lavage and analyzed biophysically. Its efficacy was evaluated in surfactant-deficient animals and in bleomycin-treated mice. In vitro, NPPS-PE effects on fibroblasts were assessed. Histological and biochemical analyses were performed to quantify collagen deposition. PE improved NPPS biophysical properties, increasing stability and surface pressure. In animal models, NPPS-PE enhanced oxygenation and reduced CO₂. In TGF-β-treated fibroblasts, NPPS-PE reduced proliferation and Col1A1 expression, and increased apoptosis. In bleomycin-treated mice, NPPS-PE significantly decreased collagen deposition and fibrosis, as shown by hydroxyproline levels and image analysis, confirming its antifibrotic potential in vivo and in vitro. PE-enriched porcine surfactant reduces fibroblast proliferation, induces apoptosis, and lowers collagen expression, showing therapeutic potential to improve respiratory function and attenuate fibrosis in pulmonary diseases.
